title: repro-EM: a reproducibility framework for materials electron microscopy
description:
Companion site for the Microscopy & Microanalysis 2026 invited talk Open Formats, Standard Metadata, and Benchmarks: A Reproducibility Framework for Materials Electron Microscopy.

Materials electron microscopy covers an unusually broad range of samples, measurements, and data dimensionalities, which has made community-wide standardization difficult. This resource argues that the mechanisms which worked for structural biology and crystallography do not depend on a common measurement, and can therefore be adopted here: open self-describing file formats with a documented, versioned layout specification; a minimal standard metadata package recorded at acquisition, including calibrations; quantitative benchmarks for data quality and reconstruction validity, including cross-validation against held-out measurements for inverse problems; and a cryptographic chain of custody running from signed detector output through to the published figure.
